protein: NEP (nuclear export protein, also NS2), a multifunctional influenza A virus protein essential for the viral life cycle
readout: Normalized log10 enrichment of the variant after one passage in MDCK-SIAT1 cells, relative to wild-type NEP
assay_method: A saturation-mutagenesis virus library spanning NEP residues 2-113 (built to avoid mutating the overlapping NS1 reading frame) was rescued and passaged once for 24 h in MDCK-SIAT1 cells. Mutation frequencies before and after passage were measured by next-generation sequencing, and fitness computed as the normalized log10 enrichment ratio, with wild-type NEP defined as 0.
remark: The reference sequence is UniProt A0ABF7SXM9, NEP of the A/WSN/1933(H1N1) strain used for the library, 121 residues; all 1894 missense labels verify against it exactly. Only positions 2 to 113 were mutagenized, so residues 1 and 114 to 121 rest on the reference sequence alone with no variant coverage. The paper's own text states 1895 of 2128 possible amino acid mutations were measured; this file has 1894, one short, after excluding the WT control row, 166 silent (synonymous, DNA-level) entries and 111 nonsense entries that the four-column format cannot represent, and 239 further missense entries with no computable enrichment value. Not extracted from this paper: the influenza RNA species (mRNA/cRNA/vRNA) quantification data, which is a separate assay on wild-type virus rather than a variant screen.
